name: Storm Surge
description: A major storm is approaching. Handle the surge in flow while maintaining effluent quality.

introMessage.title: Storm Warning!
introMessage.text:
The National Weather Service has issued a severe storm warning. Heavy rainfall is expected to begin in 2 hours and last 12+ hours. Expect significant inflow and infiltration (I&I) — flow could double or triple.

Your mission: keep the plant running and avoid permit violations. Budget your energy carefully — the storm may knock out power.

objectives.description: Review and adjust controls before the storm hits
objectives.hint: Consider increasing RAS rate and adjusting sludge wasting to manage higher flows.

objectives.description: Maintain effluent TSS below 45 mg/L during peak storm flow
objectives.hint: The secondary clarifiers will be stressed. Watch the blanket depth and SOR.

objectives.description: Complete the storm with 3 or fewer violations
objectives.hint: Some temporary exceedances are expected, but minimize them.

objectives.description: End the scenario with positive budget
objectives.hint: Storm operations use more energy. Watch your chemical costs too.

action.title: Storm Update
action.text: The storm is about 1 hour away. Barometric pressure is dropping. Consider lowering your WAS rate to build up MLSS for better settling performance.

action.title: Storm Arrives!
action.text: Heavy rainfall has begun. Flow is increasing rapidly. Monitor your clarifier blanket depths — if they rise above 40% of clarifier depth, solids will wash out.

action.title: Preparations Noted
action.text: Good — you've reviewed the controls. Now wait for the storm and be ready to react.
